$comment: Mutation arms cutting the types of package dev. Format and rules: docs/testing.md, Declared arms.

arms.name: M-SCRUB-PRIVATE-PATH-BLIND
arms.note: scrub-guard stops reading paths against the private roots, so a client file path named in the tree or in a pushed range passes the guard silently

arms.name: M-SCRUB-PRIVATE-TAIL-BLIND
arms.note: a path is read only as a whole, so a private path behind a longer lead (another checkout, a project directory) passes the guard

arms.name: M-SCRUB-PRIVATE-ABSOLUTE-BLIND
arms.note: a token may not start after a `/` again, so a private path inside an absolute, home-relative or URL path passes the guard

arms.name: M-SCRUB-PRIVATE-DOTTED-BLIND
arms.note: a dotted name names nothing, so a private module spelled as a package path passes the guard

arms.name: M-SCRUB-PRIVATE-ROOT-MODULE-BLIND
arms.note: no name counts as compound, so a private module directly under a source root passes the guard

arms.name: M-SCRUB-PRIVATE-DIRECTORY-BLIND
arms.note: a path with no extension names nothing, so a private directory passes the guard

arms.name: M-SCRUB-PRIVATE-BACKSLASH-BLIND
arms.note: a backslash is no separator, so a private path written with backslashes passes the guard

arms.name: M-SCRUB-PRIVATE-ESCAPE-BLIND
arms.note: a backslash never opens a string escape, so a private dotted path glued to a `\t` in a quoted fixture passes the guard

arms.name: M-SCRUB-LOCAL-PATH-BLIND
arms.note: scrub-guard stops reading home paths, so an added line spelling a person's home directory passes the guard

arms.name: M-SCRUB-LOCAL-PLACEHOLDER-REFUSED
arms.note: the documented placeholder name is refused like a real one, so a fixture or a doc that follows the convention is rejected

arms.name: M-SCRUB-RANGE-UNCONFIGURED-SKIPPED
arms.note: a range with no token list and no private root counts as unconfigured, so a pushed home path passes the guard on a clone that has no list

arms.name: M-SCRUB-ROW-UNCONFIGURED-FIRST
arms.replace: if (tree.err.indexOf(UNCONFIGURED) >= 0) return NotRun('unconfigured'); if (!tree.ok || !range.ok) return Failed(GateTree.quote(tree.ok ? range : tree));
arms.note: an unconfigured tree scan is read before the exit statuses, so a range that refused an added home path shows as not run

arms.name: M-DECISION-APPEND-GLUED
arms.note: a ledger that does not end in a newline gets the new decision glued onto its last line

arms.name: M-DECISION-APPEND-BLANK
arms.note: every append opens with a newline, so a ledger that already ends in one gains a blank line before each decision

arms.name: M-DECISION-NO-LENGTH-LIMIT
arms.note: a decision of any length is accepted, by the command and by the slice gate alike, and the ledger grows back into paragraphs

arms.name: M-DECISION-MULTILINE
arms.note: a text spanning several lines is appended, so one decision becomes a line plus continuations the gate cannot attribute

arms.name: M-DECISION-ANY-SLICE
arms.note: an empty slice id or a commit SHA is accepted as the slice, so a line names no slice anyone can find the merge of

arms.name: M-DECISION-GATE-NO-ARROW
arms.note: the slice gate passes an added ledger line that names no slice at all

arms.name: M-DECISION-GATE-SEES-NOTHING
arms.note: the slice gate finds no line added to the ledger, so the decisions row passes whatever a slice wrote there

arms.name: M-GATE-RENAME-UNPAIRED
arms.note: a renamed file is no longer paired with its path at the base, so the lint row compares it with nothing and every finding it carries reads as new

arms.name: M-GATE-REBASE-NONE
arms.note: a moved file's findings at the base keep their old path, so the lint row sees none of them at the new path and reports every one as new

arms.name: M-GATE-TREE-STATE-BLIND
arms.note: an infra tree's cached lint is keyed by its path alone, so a tree that changed between gate runs is compared through the lint of what it held before

arms.name: M-LAND-NOT-RUN-KEEPS-MERGE
arms.note: a pick in progress is never rolled back, so a step that threw after it, or a conflicted pick, leaves the tree mid-pick with the staged files of the branch

arms.name: M-LAND-DIVERGENCE-PATH-STAYS-QUICK
arms.note: a path where a shard and the one-process suite can diverge no longer asks for the full battery, so a slice that edits the test kit or a runtime cache lands on the quick one

arms.name: M-LAND-TENTH-LANDING-STAYS-QUICK
arms.note: the count of landings never asks for the full battery, so a run of quiet slices is never checked against the one-process suite

arms.name: M-LAND-FULL-BATTERY-SHARDS
arms.note: a full battery under a lease takes the lease's shards, so its suite adds a monolith run beside them and the land waits for both

arms.name: M-LAND-COMMIT-LOSES-AUTHOR
arms.note: the landed commit is made under whoever runs the landing, so a slice's author and date are replaced by the parent's

arms.name: M-LAND-NO-SLICE-TRAILER
arms.note: the trailer names the branch instead of the slice id, so a search for a slice by `Slice: <ID>` finds nothing

arms.name: M-LAND-ANY-NUMBER-OF-COMMITS
arms.note: a branch of several commits is accepted and only its tip is picked, so the rest of the slice is silently left behind

arms.name: M-LAND-ARMS-REGISTRY-ASKS-FULL
arms.note: a data record under the test kit is not exempt, so a landing that only moves one lands on the full battery

arms.name: M-LAND-ROLLBACK-RESETS-HARD
arms.note: a rollback discards every change of the tree, so what the user edited in a tracked file while the binaries were built is lost

arms.name: M-LAND-ROLLBACK-IGNORES-MOVED-HEAD
arms.note: a rollback resets to the commit the pick began at even when the user committed meanwhile, taking their commit off the branch

arms.name: M-LAND-LANDED-AGAIN-PASSES
arms.note: a branch landed already passes the branch check, so a second landing builds the tree and fails at an empty commit

arms.name: M-LAND-LANDED-BY-PATCH-PASSES
arms.find: if (line.startsWith('- ')) return 'a commit with the same patch';
arms.note: a branch whose patch the checked-out branch holds under a commit without the trailer is landed a second time

arms.name: M-LAND-FMT-THROW-KEEPS-REWRITE
arms.note: a writer run that throws leaves the rewritten bytes unstaged in the tree, so the rollback of the pick is refused for those files and the tree stays half-rewritten

arms.name: M-LAND-FMT-REWRITE-NOT-STAGED
arms.note: the rewrite is left unstaged, so the commit holds the unformatted bytes and the tree is dirty right after the landing

arms.name: M-LAND-FMT-NOT-NAMED
arms.note: the landing commit does not name the files the fmt step rewrote, so a reader of the history cannot tell the merge commit holds bytes the slice never wrote

arms.name: M-LAND-FMT-NON-LAYOUT-FOLDED
arms.note: every rewrite counts as layout, so a change of meaning the writer made on a merged file is folded into the landing commit unreviewed

arms.name: M-LAND-FMT-FAILURE-KEEPS-REWRITE
arms.note: a failed fmt step leaves the rewritten bytes in the tree, so the rollback of the pick is refused for those files and the tree is left half-rewritten

arms.name: M-LAND-FMT-SECOND-PASS-IGNORED
arms.note: a file the writer still rewrites after the landing's rewrite no longer fails the step, so the landed tree is one the next writer pass changes again

arms.name: M-BATTERY-BLAST-EXIT2-WAIVED
arms.note: --allow-blast also waives a lint-diff that could not compare its snapshots, so a missing or malformed base reads as a passed blast gate

arms.name: M-GATE-BRANCH-OWN-LEASE
arms.note: a gate's branch inside a workflow asks the pool for its own threads although its gate already leased them, so the branch's build and suite take a second lease or wait behind their own gate

arms.name: M-GATE-DEMAND-LISTS-NONE
arms.note: the branch of the short rows holds no thread in a gate run, so the heavy branch asks for the thread the lists, fmt and scrub rows run on and the gate oversubscribes the pool

arms.name: M-GATE-ARTIFACT-BASE-SIZE-DROPPED
arms.note: a base size that never reaches the row makes every touched large file count as added, so an unchanged or slightly grown one fails the gate

arms.name: M-SWEEP-FIX-RESULT-IGNORED
arms.note: an engine lint --fix that failed reads as a fix that changed nothing

arms.name: M-SWEEP-FORMAT-UNCHECKED
arms.note: a probe the formatter changed is judged only by its fix, compared with the formatted text

arms.name: M-SWEEP-TRACE-LINE-COMPARED
arms.note: a trace's file:line prefix is compared, so a formatter that moves a call reads as one that changed the program

arms.name: M-EDGEDIFF-LIBRARY-BARE-FULLPATH
arms.note: the project side keys by a bare fullPath, null for a missing path, so a missing project file and every missing library file look alike and the library filter drops or keeps the wrong files

arms.name: M-BASE-ENGINE-CHECKSUM-BLIND
arms.note: a cached base engine is reused without checking its content against its checksum, so a damaged or truncated engine answers every parity run

arms.name: M-PARITY-EXIT-BLIND
arms.note: parity no longer compares exit statuses, so an engine that starts refusing an invocation with the same output reads as equal

arms.name: M-PROBE-EXIT-BLIND
arms.note: a probe kit no longer compares exit statuses, so an engine that starts refusing an invocation with the same streams and no write reads as matching its recording

arms.name: M-PROBE-KNOWN-DEFECT-COUNTED
arms.note: a known-defect row that moved counts as a deviation, so a fix to a defect the kit recorded fails the probe like a regression

arms.name: M-PROBE-ONE-PASS-BLIND
arms.note: a formatter row whose second pass rewrites its own output still reads as one pass

arms.name: M-PROBE-SAME-RUN-BLIND
arms.note: a fix that changes what the program prints still reads as the same run

arms.name: M-GATE-ARMS-NEIGHBOUR-BLIND
arms.note: the arms row stops widening to call neighbours, so a change to a member the arm's member calls makes its pin blind and the slice lands green

arms.name: M-GATE-ARMS-NEIGHBOUR-UNWIRED
arms.note: the row's selection still takes neighbours but nothing hands it any, so no arm on a call neighbour of a changed member ever runs

arms.name: M-GATE-ARMS-EXIT-IGNORED
arms.note: a run that fails after a clean tally passes the row, so the tally hides whatever went wrong behind it

arms.name: M-ARM-RENDER-FAILURE-REFUSES
arms.replace:
if (job.applyOnly) return reportApplied(rendered.length, applyFail);
	if (applyFail.length > 0) return refuse(applyFail);
arms.note: a run that refuses at the first arm that does not render takes the whole registry down with it

arms.name: M-GATE-ARMS-UNRENDERED-PASSES
arms.note: an arm whose cut did not render is no track, so a waived survivor can make the tally add up and pass an arm that never ran

arms.name: M-GATE-ARMS-ROT-UNREAD
arms.note: a survivor is never read again at the base, so rot the slice did not cause reads as its own and the worker bisects it by hand

arms.name: M-GATE-ARMS-LEASE-UNNAMED
arms.note: a row that fails or passes names no thread count, so a rot read on one thread looks like the base's rot to a pin that needs parallel work

arms.name: M-GATE-ARMS-BASE-THREADS-UNGUARDED
arms.note: a base that was not read, or had no survivor to read, is reported as a base run that held threads

arms.name: M-GATE-ARMS-THREADS-OUT-OF-EXCERPT
arms.note: the threads line is only in the failed message, which the clip cuts, so a long row loses the lease the reader needs

arms.name: M-GATE-ARMS-WAIVER-IGNORED
arms.note: --allow-arm changes nothing, so a parent can only waive the whole row and hide the slice's own arms

arms.name: M-GATE-BRANCH-DROPS-WAIVER
arms.note: the gate's waivers never reach the arms branch, the process that reads them

arms.name: M-GATE-FMT-CROSS-HALF-IGNORED
arms.note: a slice whose touched file needs two rewrites under the cross-config passes the gate's fmt row and turns the battery red after the merge

arms.name: M-GATE-CHECK-DROPS-ARMS-PHASE
arms.note: a gate run that never starts the arms phase reports no arms row, so an arm that no longer kills its pin passes

arms.name: M-GATE-ARMS-RUN-ON-RED-ROW
arms.note: a gate whose first fan-out already has a red row still starts the arms kill run, spending its minutes on a verdict the gate has already given

arms.name: M-GATE-ARMS-LEASE-BEFORE-PLAN
arms.note: an arms phase that does not ask the plan first leases and starts a branch for a selection that is empty

arms.name: M-GATE-ALLOW-IGNORED
arms.note: a row named by --allow still fails, so a slice that must carry an offending file cannot pass its gate

arms.name: M-GATE-SETTLED-ARMS-ROW-DROPPED
arms.note: a plan the gate settles in its own process never reaches the table, so a mistyped --arm passes the gate

arms.name: M-GATE-ARMS-PLAN-THROWS-IN-GATE
arms.find: return try GateArms.plan(_gate) catch (_: Exception) null;
arms.note: a plan that cannot be made ends the gate after every other row has run, instead of failing the arms row

arms.name: M-GATE-REGISTRY-REFUSAL-DROPPED
arms.note: an arm registry that does not read shows only as branches that never ran, not as the cause

arms.name: M-GATE-REGISTRY-REFUSAL-WAIVABLE
arms.note: --allow arms would turn the refusal into a pass of a gate that ran no other row

arms.name: M-GATE-REGISTRY-REFUSAL-READS-NOARMS
arms.note: --no-arms must leave the registry unread

arms.name: M-GATE-BASELINE-RECORDED-AFTER-FAILURE
arms.note: a baseline taken with a failed row is written and the gate compares with it as if it were whole

arms.name: M-GATE-BASELINE-NOT-RETIRED
arms.note: a baseline run that fails leaves the previous baseline and the base suite reading kept beside it in place, and the gate compares with the older base

arms.name: M-GATE-CORPUS-FORK-NOT-CHECKED
arms.note: a corpus fork that names no directory is not named as the cause of the missing snapshot

arms.name: M-GATE-CORPUS-SNAPSHOT-NOT-CHECKED
arms.note: the corpus row goes on to save or compare a snapshot the suite never wrote

arms.name: M-GATE-CORPUS-BASE-UNREAD
arms.find: case Unread(why): return NotRun(GateTree.clip('no corpus snapshot of the base: $why'));
arms.note: a base suite that could not be read is not named as the cause of the missing base corpus snapshot

arms.name: M-GATE-STALE-SNAPSHOT-KEPT
arms.note: a snapshot an earlier run left in the tree stands for the suite that just ran

arms.name: M-ARM-DELETES-CALLER-FORK
arms.note: a full run in the caller's process unsets the corpus fork for every later suite of that runner, which then writes no sweep snapshot

arms.name: M-CHECK-SLOT-KEEPS-FORK
arms.note: the slot processes of a mutation run inherit the caller's corpus fork, so an arm verdict depends on the shell it was started from

arms.name: M-SLOT-DRAWS-NO-FREE-PORT
arms.note: a mutation slot draws a candidate without asking which port may be taken, so its client connects to whatever holds it before the next attempt

arms.name: M-BATTERY-SNAPSHOT-KEPT
arms.note: the suite runs over the previous run's corpus snapshot, so a suite in which no corpus case ran compares an old sweep with the base and the head is saved with it

arms.name: M-GATE-ARMS-ASK-UNBOUNDED
arms.note: the arms lease asks for the top of its range whatever the kill run's track count, so a selection under the top holds threads no slot can use and a single track waits the whole-share window that closes the pool to every waiter behind it

arms.name: M-GATE-ARMS-ASK-IGNORES-PLAN
arms.note: the arms lease asks for the top of its range whatever the plan selected, so a one-arm selection waits for a whole share it cannot use and closes the pool to the waiters behind it

arms.name: M-SWEEP-FILES-OWN-TEXT-LOST
arms.note: a trap's file wins over the probe's own text

arms.name: M-GATE-REUSE-NOTHING-TAKEN
arms.note: no gate record stands for any battery row, so a land of the very tree its gate passed runs the whole battery again

arms.name: M-GATE-REUSE-TREE-BLIND
arms.note: a gate record stands for a land whatever tree it merged, so a slice landed onto a main that moved since its gate skips the rows that never saw main's new commit

arms.name: M-GATE-REUSE-SKIPPED-COVERS
arms.note: every gate row counts as passed, so a row the gate skipped or could not run is taken over by the land as if it had been measured

arms.name: M-GATE-REUSE-FAIL-TRUSTED
arms.note: the record of a red gate stands for the land's rows, so a slice whose gate failed lands with the rows that passed read off it

arms.name: M-GATE-REUSE-LOCATE-ANY
arms.note: the first worktree holding any branch answers, so a land reads the record of another worktree's gate or none at all

arms.name: M-BATTERY-REUSED-SWEEP-IGNORED
arms.note: a battery that took the suite over from the gate still reads its own tree's corpus snapshot, which no suite of this run wrote, so the corpus row fails and the snapshot of the next base loses its sweep

arms.name: M-GATE-REUSE-MOVED-TREE-PASSES
arms.note: a check whose worktree got a commit or an amend while its rows ran still records a pass, for a tree no row measured, and a land of that tree skips the rows

arms.name: M-GATE-ARMS-MEMBER-BLIND
arms.note: the arms row selects every arm of a touched type again, so a change to one member of a macro file costs every arm on it

arms.name: M-GATE-ARMS-UNNAMED-MEMBERS-NARROWED
arms.note: a module whose changed members the report cannot name selects none of its arms, so a type-header or whole-type change lands with no arm run

arms.name: M-GATE-ARMS-PIN-HELPER-BLIND
arms.note: a changed helper of a test class no longer reaches the pins of the class, so a fixture weakened through its helper meets no killer

arms.name: M-CHANGED-MEMBERS-NONMEMBER-NAMED
arms.find: final member: Null<String> = MEMBER_KINDS.contains(kind) ? name : null;
arms.note: a named row of a non-member kind (a type's header, a parameter) is read as a member, so a file whose change cannot be told member by member names members and the arms of the others are dropped

arms.name: M-PARITY-ONE-PROCESS-UNASKED
arms.note: one process is chosen whenever it is wanted, so an engine built before the batch entry fails every invocation of a probe or parity run instead of running each in its own process

arms.name: M-PROBE-FAILURE-DROPPED
arms.note: a deviating row no longer names why the engine gave no answer, so a failed batch share reads as empty streams

arms.name: M-GATE-REUSE-NODE-BLIND
arms.note: a gate record stands for a land under another node, or for an older record that names none, so a node upgrade between the gate and the land takes rows measured by the old runtime

arms.name: M-ARM-COMPOSABLE-TOOLS-REFUSED
arms.note: a tool's arm is built on its own again, one test.js per arm the schema could have carried

arms.name: M-ARM-COMPOSABLE-MACRO-ALLOWED
arms.note: a compile-time arm is composed, so its switch is reached while the composed build compiles and the arm waits minutes for a build it cannot use

arms.name: M-ARM-COMPOSABLE-BUILT-FILE-ALLOWED
arms.note: a file a @:build macro reads is composed, so the macro sees the copies as fields of the type it reads

arms.name: M-SCHEMA-BUILD-EMBEDDED-ROOT-KEPT
arms.note: an embedded module of tool code is typed under the name tools.src.dev.E, which names no module, so its copy is never checked in the macro context

arms.name: M-GATE-REUSE-IMPACT-SUITE-TAKEN
arms.note: a land takes over the suite a gate ran on the classes its change reaches, so a slice lands with most of the suite never run on its tree

arms.name: M-SHARD-SUBSET-REFRESHES-WEIGHTS
arms.note: a subset run rewrites the class weights with its own few classes, so the next whole run deals every other class by the default weight

arms.name: M-SUITE-IMPACT-NOTHING-REACHED
arms.note: a change reaches no test class, so a gate passes a slice whose tests never ran

arms.name: M-SUITE-IMPACT-MACRO-BOUNDED
arms.note: a change of the macros, the runtime, a grammar or the test kit runs only the classes that name it, though generated code reaches every class

arms.name: M-SUITE-IMPACT-STATE-BLIND
arms.note: a helper that leaves an environment variable or a working directory behind runs only the classes that name it, though it reaches every class in its shard's process

arms.name: M-SUITE-IMPACT-MACRO-DEPENDENT-BOUNDED
arms.note: a module a macro depends on runs only the classes that name it, though the macro's generated code reaches classes that never name the module

arms.name: M-SUITE-IMPACT-RUNNER-BOUNDED
arms.note: a change of the runner every class runs inside runs only the classes that name it

arms.name: M-SUITE-IMPACT-UNPARSED-BOUNDED
arms.note: a source that does not parse declares no types, so a same-package file using one of them is never reached

arms.name: M-GATE-CORPUS-SHORTFALL-SKIPPED
arms.note: an impact run whose corpus class ran and wrote no snapshot leaves the corpus row skipped, so a broken harness passes the gate

arms.name: M-GATE-CORPUS-FORK-SKIPPED
arms.note: a fork that names no directory leaves an impact run's corpus row skipped instead of failing the misconfiguration

arms.name: M-NARROW-CLASSES-NONE
arms.note: no track gets a narrow build, so every arm types the whole suite again

arms.name: M-NARROW-CLASSES-SKIPS-UNKNOWN
arms.note: an expectation naming no test class is dropped from the narrow build, which then cannot run it

arms.name: M-NARROW-KILL-UNGUARDED
arms.note: a narrow kill is taken over a base that is red without the cut, so a class failing outside the full registry reads as a kill

arms.name: M-NARROW-IN-BUILD-ONLY
arms.note: a build-only run (--check-apply) takes the narrow build, so a cut that breaks a class outside its pins closure no longer reads BUILD-FAIL there

arms.name: M-SUITE-IMPACT-ARM-MISS-BLIND
arms.note: a pinned class the impact selection leaves out of an arm's file is not reported, so the census passes an arm whose killer an impact suite would never run

arms.name: M-SUITE-IMPACT-ARM-WHOLE-MISSED
arms.note: an arm whose file runs every class is reported as missing its pins, so a census cries for arms on the macros and the runtime that no selection can miss

arms.name: M-SUITE-IMPACT-GRAPH-LEAKS-BETWEEN-FILES
arms.note: a graph read for one file keeps its reach into the next, so the census, which shares one graph across every arm, widens a later selection and hides the misses it exists to find

arms.name: M-POSTLAND-RED-RECORD-REFUSES-NOTHING
arms.note: a red whole-suite record refuses nothing, so a land goes on over a main whose landed commit is known red

arms.name: M-POSTLAND-STARTS-AFTER-WHOLE-BATTERY
arms.note: a land whose battery already ran the whole suite starts a second whole suite after it

arms.name: M-POSTLAND-GREEN-KEEPS-LOG
arms.note: a green whole-suite run leaves its log in the cache, one file per impact land for good

arms.name: M-POSTLAND-RED-KEEPS-SCRIPT
arms.note: a finished run leaves its copy of the tool in the cache, one large file per impact land for good

arms.name: M-POSTLAND-LAUNCH-PID-LOST
arms.note: a started run is recorded under no pid, so a live whole-suite run reads as lost and a land starts a second one beside it

arms.name: M-POSTLAND-CLEAR-LOST
arms.note: post-land clear leaves the records of a lost run behind, so the same commit is reported lost until the cache is swept by hand

arms.name: M-POSTLAND-LOST-RESTARTS
arms.note: a land goes on over a lost run without starting its whole suite again, so the landed commit is never verified by a whole suite

arms.name: M-POSTLAND-DEAD-PID-READS-LOST
arms.note: every run record counts as running, so a run whose process is gone is never reported lost and a land never starts it again

arms.name: M-LAND-IMPACT-SCOPE-IGNORED
arms.note: the impact of the merge is never asked, so every land runs every test class under the lock as before

arms.name: M-LAND-WHOLE-SCOPE-STARTS-POST-LAND
arms.note: a change no text bounds runs the whole suite under the lock and then runs it a second time after the land

arms.name: M-BATTERY-IMPACT-DISPATCH-DROPPED
arms.note: the suite row ignores the list of classes it was given and runs every class, so an impact land pays for the whole suite under the lock

arms.name: M-SUITE-IMPACT-ENV-KEY-WIDE
arms.note: a file that sets an environment key no other file spells runs every class, so a tool that exports a variable only it reads costs a whole suite

arms.name: M-SUITE-IMPACT-ENV-RUNNER-KEY-BOUNDED
arms.note: a file that sets an environment key the runner, the test kit, a macro or generated code reads runs only the classes that name it, though the next class in its process meets the key

arms.name: M-SUITE-IMPACT-ENV-READER-BLIND
arms.note: a file that sets an environment key runs only the classes that name it, not the ones that read the key it sets

arms.name: M-SUITE-IMPACT-ENV-INTERPOLATED-KEY-LITERAL
arms.note: an environment key spelled with an interpolation is taken for a literal no file spells, so a file that sets a key it computes runs only the classes that name it

arms.name: M-SUITE-IMPACT-ENV-LATER-CALL-DROPPED
arms.note: only the first environment key a file sets is read, so a key set by a later call and read by the runner side leaves the suite bounded

arms.name: M-SUITE-IMPACT-WHY-READER-BLIND
arms.note: the why answer ignores the readers of an environment key a touched file sets, so it calls not reached a class the scope selects

arms.name: M-LAND-WARM-THROW-FAILS-LAND
arms.force: start == null ? Skipped('no baseline warm requested') : start(repo, head)
arms.note: a baseline warm that cannot start throws through the land step, so a green land is rolled back for a background measurement

arms.name: M-WARM-MOVED-KEEPS-GATE
arms.note: a baseline warm whose commit is no longer the tip leaves its gate running to the end, holding the pool for an entry no new slice will ask for

arms.name: M-WARM-SETTLE-KEEPS-SCRIPT
arms.note: a finished baseline warm leaves its copy of dev.js behind in the cache, a few megabytes for every warmed land

arms.name: M-BASESUITE-ENGINE-NOT-BUILT
arms.note: the base checkout's suite runs without the engine its tests spawn, and ten of them fail on a clean base

arms.name: M-BASESUITE-ENGINE-UNPINNED
arms.note: the base suite's tests run the engine of the tree under gate, not the base's own

arms.name: M-BASESUITE-ENGINE-LEAKS
arms.note: the base checkout's engine stays pinned in the gate process after the base suite ends

arms.name: M-BASESUITE-IMPACT-READS-BASE
arms.note: an impact gate builds and runs a whole base suite for a delta it never prints

arms.name: M-BASESUITE-RED-GATE-READS-BASE
arms.note: a red gate suite still pays for a base suite

arms.name: M-BASESUITE-DELTA-DROPPED
arms.note: a whole-suite gate with a readable base prints no counts beside the base's

arms.name: M-JVM-PROBE-CPP-IGNORED
arms.note: --cpp no longer picks the hxcpp pair, so dev jvm-portability --cpp builds and runs the --jvm probe

arms.name: M-JVM-PROBE-CPP-DROPS-PATHS
arms.note: the hxcpp run drops its paths and always reads the default scope

arms.name: M-GATE-ARMS-FLOOR-BLIND
arms.note: a selection over the floor keeps every pin-killer and call-neighbour arm in the kill run, so a sweep over hundreds of files pays a build per arm for claims that only a changed member of the arm makes decisive

arms.name: M-GATE-ARMS-DEMOTED-DROPPED
arms.note: an arm moved out of the kill run by the floor is not apply-checked either, so a rotted cut among them passes the row unseen

arms.name: M-GATE-ARMS-CARRY-BLIND
arms.note: a re-gate of the same tree re-runs every arm the last gate killed, so one error in a fix round costs the whole kill run again

arms.name: M-GATE-ARMS-CARRY-RECORD-BLIND
arms.note: a re-gate carries an arm whose record was re-encoded since the last kill run, so the new cut is never run

arms.name: M-GATE-ARMS-CARRY-RERUN-BLIND
arms.note: a re-gate carries an arm the changes since the last kill run reach, so a fix round that weakens its pin passes unseen

arms.name: M-GATE-ARMS-CARRY-UNWIRED
arms.note: the arms row never reads the last kill run, so the carry exists only as a function nobody calls

arms.name: M-GATE-ARMS-MEMO-UNWRITTEN
arms.note: a kill run leaves no record of the arms it killed, so no re-gate can carry one

arms.name: M-GATE-ARMS-MEMO-DIRTY
arms.note: a kill run of a tree with uncommitted edits is recorded under HEAD, so the next gate carries arms killed against a state HEAD does not hold

arms.name: M-GATE-ARMS-MEMO-NEGATIVE
arms.note: the memo records every selected arm with no failing row as killed, so a track the tally counts but that printed no row is carried and a failed arms row turns green on a re-gate of the same HEAD

arms.name: M-GATE-ARMS-MEMO-SURVIVOR
arms.note: every printed track row counts as a kill, so a survivor or a waived arm is carried by the next gate and never run again

arms.name: M-GATE-ARMS-CARRY-ASKED-BLIND
arms.note: an arm asked for with --arm can be carried out of the kill run, and the row then fails naming an arm it had selected

arms.name: M-BASE-LINT-NEEDED-ALWAYS
arms.note: every gate lints the base for INFRA gate 4, also one that moved no rule code or whose baseline names no infra tree

arms.name: M-BASE-LINT-KEPT-BLIND
arms.note: a base lint kept in the logs or in the cache the worktrees share is never taken, so every rule-code gate lints its base again

arms.name: M-BASE-BRANCH-READ-MEASURES-BESIDE
arms.note: a row asking while the base branch runs measures the base again beside it instead of waiting for what the branch leaves

arms.name: M-BASE-BRANCH-SETTLE-FORGETS-WHY
arms.note: a failed base branch lifts its announcement without leaving why, so a row asking afterwards measures the base a second time

arms.name: M-GATE-BASELINE-LINTS-BASE
arms.note: a --baseline run lints again, serially before the first gate, what a rule-code gate reads from BaseLint beside its rows

arms.name: M-GATE-BASE-LINT-NOT-STARTED
arms.note: a rule-code gate starts no base lint branch, so its infra4 row lints the base itself, behind its own lints

arms.name: M-WARM-BASE-LINT-STAMP-OFF
arms.note: the warm keeps the base lint under a key no gate on the landed commit asks for, so every land lints for nothing and every first rule-code gate lints its base again

arms.name: M-PARITY-NODE-FLAGS-RESPELT
arms.note: the batch process runs node with a constant instead of the flags bin/apq carries, so a changed shim flag leaves parity and probe on the old one

arms.name: M-PARITY-PRESET-RESPELT
arms.note: the hxq argv prefix is spelled in the tool instead of read from bin/hxq, so a changed preset reaches a batch process only after a hand edit

arms.name: M-PARITY-SHIM-LINE-SILENT
arms.find: if (!row.match(File.getContent(file))) throw new Exception('$file has no line matching ${row}');
arms.note: a shim without the line parity reads answers no words instead of failing, so a batch process runs without the node flags or the hxq preset while a call through the shim keeps them
